chapter: Miles Davis stories and what jazz means
title: What is jazz? The word as a museum term
summary: Gil declines to define jazz and says the word will become historical like other labels.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Yes, and you can talk kind of freely about jazz that because.....

I wouldn't want to describe jazz verbally any more then to just to play all the records that have been made by people, of music that isn't that isn't of the past and rhythmically it's not of the past.
Well then the meaning, it has expanded whatever it meant originally would you say?

I wouldn't try to even think about describing as defining jazz. Now most people, a lot of people now don't want to use the word jazz any more and there's really no use being militant about it because it's going to become a museum-type word anyway. It's going to become, going to go into the museum like the classical era, and the romantic and symphony music era and rag time. All these eras, those things become historical, right? They go into the museum and become historical. So, as far as using the word jazz now, if you don't want to you don't have to.

A lot of it has to do with the commercial value of it. Sometimes the people think they can do better if they call it jazz. Or they can do better if they don't call it jazz. So there is an eye towards the currency, right?
I'm wondering if it's as much currency now as it is the......
All currency. The currency of music and the currency of the money.
